cells.tense: You are here with the pen and the picture is still moving.
cells.act: tend the fire without burning out
cells.ask: Give twenty minutes this week to whatever you're most looking forward to. No plan for after. Just the time, and then notice what it asks of you next.
cells.core:
You feel what wants to happen before it does, and you move toward it without a plan. That openness is working. You catch a mood shift and add or pull back before anyone says a word, and the flow holds because you stayed with it.

Tending the fire means give one thing your full attention here. Pick what you've been looking forward to most, give it twenty minutes, and don't plan past that. If you're afraid the twenty minutes will ask for more, let the week show you whether that fear is true or just a story. What you'll have is a direction you can feel, not one you decided.

cells.tense: You will be sensing the next room before this one has finished changing.
cells.act: learn how it grows by tending it
cells.ask: Pause the project you're most excited about for three days. On the fourth, work on it for ten minutes and stop. See whether the wish stays warm while you wait.
cells.core:
The sensing has run past the room. You feel what hasn't happened yet and brace for it, so the adjustment gets made before there's anything to adjust to. It looks like attunement from the inside. From where others stand, it reads as being set against a room that hasn't changed.

Tending a thing to learn how it grows is a deliberate slowdown. Take the project or plan you're most excited about and pause it three days. On the fourth, work on it for ten minutes and stop. The gap is doing the work. If the wish stays warm when you come back, it belongs to you and not to the bracing.

cells.tense: You have been feeling what was happening and not what is here now.
cells.act: perceive it with fresh eyes before judging
cells.ask: Sit with something you usually pass over — ten minutes, no plan, no telling anyone. Let it stay unfamiliar longer than feels comfortable.
cells.core:
The sensing is turned toward what already happened. You know what a room was going to do, how the mood shifted last time, what the adjustment should have been, and the information arrives after the moment has passed. The feeling is intact. The arrival is late.

Perceiving with fresh eyes is a way back in. Sit with something you usually pass over — a corner, a sound, a page — for ten minutes, without settling what it is and without telling anyone. Let it stay unfamiliar. When the feeling comes back online, you'll know by the fact that the room feels like it's happening now instead of running behind you.

cells.tense: The feeling is running and you are calling it something that happens to you.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Take one moment you read recently and set it on paper in plain order, no feeling words. Read it once. That page is yours; the reading back is the act.
cells.core:
The sensing is doing its work, and your name is not on it. You read the room and make the adjustment, then file the whole thing under the mood or the day or the other person. The tuning is happening. The credit has gone missing.

Putting the inquiry on paper brings the credit back. Take one moment you read recently and set it on paper in plain order, no feeling words in it. Read it once and stop. You'll see your own hand in what happened — the adjustment and the timing of it — and the page will show you the work you've been refusing to own.
